articles.title: Week 9 Fantasy Football Early Waiver Wire Pickups: Tyler Allgeier, Adonai Mitchell among top adds
articles.summary: We go over some useful fantasy football waiver wire pickups before we get into Week 9.
articles.body:
Well, that was an interesting early window in the Week 8 fantasy football slate. Things were looking pretty bleak in the first half of games before a flurry of fantasy points and exciting finishes came in the second half. There's still plenty of action left but we're already thinking ahead to Week 9 as we hit the halfway mark of the 2026 NFL season. Below are some early waiver wire pickups to consider as we head into next week.

Tyler Allgeier, RB, Cardinals (52% rostered)

Allgeier climbs just over the usual threshold we use for roster percentage with this waiver piece. But we'll make an exception given his Week 8 performance. We had been looking for this type of game the previous two weeks with rookie Jeremiyah Love banged up. Instead, it was Bam Knight who stepped up and performed well.

But in Week 8, things shifted big time. Love and Knight both got injured against the Cowboys and it forced Arizona to lean on Allgeier, who did not disappoint. He had one of the most efficient games by a back we've ever seen, taking just 16 touches (five catches) for 191 total yards and two touchdowns. Allgeier finished with 36.60 fantasy points; he had a combined 40 fantasy points in the previous seven games. If Love and Knight are out, Allgeier is in the RB2/3 conversation moving forward. Just know next week's matchup against the Seahawks is not ideal.

Adonai Mitchell, WR, Jets (11% rostered)

We had pretty much written off Mitchell after last week. He must have gotten offended. After returning from injury, AD put up a goose egg on three targets in Week 7 against the Dolphins. Rookie Omar Cooper Jr. had a second straight 20+ fantasy-point outing.

Well, the roles reversed in Week 8 against the Raiders.

Cooper was non-existent, finishing the game without a target. Mitchell, on the other hand, led the receiving group with a 7-142-1 line for 23.7 fantasy points, finishing the 1 p.m. ET Sunday window as the WR1 overall. This Jets passing game is clearly going to be tough to crack. Garrett Wilson voiced frustration after last week's game and saw 10 targets this week. The Cooper disappearing act, you'd think, won't become the norm.

Mitchell looked too good to leave on the wire in deeper formats. He may be volatile but we know what his ceiling looks like when peppered with targets. Mitchell will be a decent WR3/flex option moving forward, though the Chiefs on the road next week aren't a great draw.

Ryan Flournoy, WR, Cowboys (34% rostered on Yahoo)

Yahoo analyst Scott Pianowski loves his carnival teams and the Cowboys have been exactly that this season — good offense, bad defense. So, with a strong offense and passing game come multiple pass-catchers who can thrive. Flournoy is carving out a nice role as the third option behind CeeDee Lamb and George Pickens. There's clear chemistry with QB Dak Prescott as well, developed over the past three seasons.

Flournoy now has two touchdowns in the past three games and has at least nine fantasy points in four straight weeks. He's also not a bad bench stash considering what his role would become if something were to happen to Lamb or Pickens, the latter of whom was questionable going into Week 8 (but active). Despite being the third option, Flournoy is a useful flex in PPR formats, and a receiver who has upside as we head into the second half of the season.

If Week 8 was the last game for Jonathan Taylor in a Colts uniform, that would be kind of sad. Indy got demolished on the road by the Jaguars on Sunday, and JT finished with just 47 total yards on 12 touches, also losing a fumble. The rookie McGowan had only five carries for 29 yards, but you've got to think the Colts could make some more deals after this dismal performance.

If Taylor gets traded before Week 9, McGowan would likely be thrust into the featured back role. Second-year player DJ Giddens is the only other back on the roster right now. If McGowan is taken in your league, Giddens isn't a bad add either. He ended up getting some garbage-time runs, finishing with 31 yards on four carries.

Starting running backs don't grow on trees for fantasy, so being able to snag a potential starter off the waiver wire this late into the season is an opportunity you can't pass up. The Colts are still very bad, so temper expectations for McGowan, but the seventh-rounder should get a long look and could see upwards of double-digit touches per week.

articles.title: Kimi Antonelli becomes youngest Formula 1 champion ever at 20 years old
articles.summary: The Italian prodigy clinched the 2026 world championship in Mexico, vanquishing his rivals from contention with four races still on the calendar.
articles.body:
Kimi Antonelli clinched the Formula 1 world championship Sunday, becoming at just 20 the youngest driver in the sport's history to win the title.

The Italian prodigy secured the title at the Mexican Grand Prix with four races left on the 2026 calendar , capping a sensational season in just his second year in F1.

He finished third and scored 15 points, enough to vanquish his remaining rivals from mathematical contention for the most coveted trophy in motor racing.

"We did it! Thank you so much," an emotional Antonelli said on the team radio after he took the checkered flag.

"I'm very grateful for this moment," he said after he jumped out of the car. "It's one that will live forever. I'm speechless. I'm trying to process what has just happened. ... Looking forward to some more battles in the future."

Antonelli broke the record set by Sebastian Vettel, who was 23 when he won the championship in a title-deciding thriller in 2010. Antonelli also became Italy's first F1 world champion since Alberto Ascari in 1953, vaulting him to superstardom at home.

Antonelli has won nine of 19 races so far this season, consistently outperforming his veteran Mercedes teammate and chief rival, George Russell, who began the year as the betting favorite to win the 2026 championship.

Red Bull's Max Verstappen won Sunday's race. Ferrari's Lewis Hamilton started on pole position and finished second. Russell qualified second but finished sixth Sunday after a 10-second time penalty for a crash ruined his race. Russell and Hamilton both needed to win — and have Antonelli finish lower down the order — to have any chance of staying in the title fight.

It was a poetic moment for Antonelli, sharing a podium with Hamilton and Verstappen, two legends of the sport who have won seven and four world championships, respectively.

At the opening race of the season in Australia, Russell seemed to solidify his front-running status with a victory, as Mercedes fulfilled expectations by building the fastest car under the new regulations that began this year. But from there, it has all been downhill for Russell, 28, as Antonelli won the next five races to establish himself as the clear favorite.

"Kimi surprised us all with his maturity. Obviously we knew he had speed and all this talent. I think not many people expected that he was, this year, so quick and beating a very strong teammate like George," former Haas F1 team principal Guenther Steiner told NBC News. "I didn't expect it. He's a 20-year-old with the mind of a 30-year-old experienced F1 driver. That made him what he is."

Antonelli took the lead of the championship in the third race of the 2026 season, and he never relinquished it. A critical juncture came when he won in Canada and Monaco while Russell failed to score points in either race because of a mechanical failure and a pit-timing error by F1. Antonelli's lead ballooned to 68 points after the sixth race.

Antonelli had some bad luck of his own in subsequent races, and Russell made up ground. But it wasn't enough. And as Russell has acknowledged, Antonelli has outperformed him throughout the season, with more pole positions and race wins, as well as superior speed when both drivers had an equal opportunity.

Another former F1 team boss, Otmar Szafnauer, said Antonelli's championship-winning season can be attributed to three things: "his mental preparedness, raw talent and great attitude."

"He is able to mentally compartmentalize to his advantage," Szafnauer told NBC News, by staying consistent under pressure.

Antonelli all but guaranteed his title last Sunday with a victory in Austin, Texas, prompting even his rivals to concede defeat.

"The truth is he's been at a higher level than me this year," Russell told reporters Thursday.

"This season, we have the best car, and I'm not able to achieve these results. So, yeah, it's quite strange and certainly has us scratching our heads a little bit," he said.

After four years in a Mercedes that was capable only of occasional wins, Russell finally got his title-winning car. But it was Antonelli who made the most of it. The new generation of F1 cars — with less downforce and more reliance on electrical power — has forced competitors to rethink their driving styles.

The new cars reward Antonelli's aggressive style of braking late and attacking corners with sharp turns. He's also more comfortable than others driving at the limit with a loose-handling car that tends to slide underneath him.

By contrast, the 2026 cars punish Russell's preference for smoother inputs and gaining lap time by getting on the throttle early on corner exits. That approach, which served him well in the previous generation of cars, eats up tire life and battery power in the newer machines. Russell has said adjusting his approach feels "like a golfer changing his swing."

The defining moment of the rivalry came at the Italian Grand Prix, when Antonelli started 19th and hunted down Russell to win the race. It was a statement victory that underscored his advantage over his teammate.

Last Sunday in Austin, Antonelli told NBC News he still hadn't reached his full potential and discussed areas where he could improve, including race starts and his tendency to exceed "track limits" and incur penalties or warnings.

"Track limits has been the bigger thing for me," he said. "But definitely, these kinds of situations, and then also in some of the qualifying sessions, I just didn't go in with the right mindset. So, yeah, just making sure I improve those."

The reversal of the Mercedes driver hierarchy has been the shock of the season. Antonelli had an up-and-down rookie season last year, showing flashes of brilliance and stretches of struggle. He was comprehensively outperformed in 2025 by Russell, who was widely seen as a champion-in-waiting, ready to strike when he had a car strong enough to win regularly.

Antonelli's triumph leaves several contenders battling for second place in the standings, with Russell, Hamilton, Verstappen and Charles Leclerc all in close contention.

Russell said finishing second in 2026 matters less to him than setting himself up to compete for a title next year.

"For every driver on the grid, there's only one position that matters, and it's P1," he told reporters. "Of course, I want to finish as high as possible. ... What's more important to me is to finish the season with positive momentum rather than necessarily that final order."

articles.title: Kimi Antonelli Makes F1 History with 1st-Ever World Title After Mexico Grand Prix Finish
articles.summary: Kimi Antonelli made history after clinching the Formula 1 world title on Sunday.
articles.body:
Kimi Antonelli made history after clinching the Formula 1 world title on Sunday.

At 20 years old, Antonelli is now the youngest champion in F1 after earning enough points by finishing in the No. 3 spot at the Mexico City Grand Prix.

Sebastian Vettel previously held the record by becoming a world champion at 23 years and 134 days old in 2010, per ESPN's Nate Saunders .

As for Antonelli, he won the drivers' championship in just his second year of F1 competition after replacing Lewis Hamilton at Mercedes in 2025.

"We did it," Antonelli said after Sunday's race, per Formula1.com . "You know, without them, I wouldn't be here – without Mercedes, without my family. So I'm very grateful for this moment, and it's one that will live forever. I'm speechless. I'm trying to process what has just happened."

"This weekend I did feel a bit more tense, but I'm just so happy, and happy that we got it done, and now we can enjoy the rest of the season," he added.

Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton finished ahead of Antonelli at the Mexico Grand Prix, although they lifted the 20-year-old up on their shoulders at the podium to celebrate his accomplishment.

Antonelli also became the first F1 world champion from Italy since Alberto Ascari in 1953.

articles.title: David Beckham earns over $23,000 a day from fragrances as his business reports $7 million in profit
articles.summary: David Beckham has found a way to keep scoring financially long after hanging up his football boots.
articles.body: David Beckham has found a way to keep scoring financially long after hanging up his football boots. The former Manchester United and Real Madrid star has transformed his sporting fame into a powerful business brand, and his fragrance company is proving particularly profitable. According to financial accounts reported by MARCA on October 27, 2026, the business recorded $8.3 million in turnover last year, averaging more than $23,000 in daily revenue. With millions flowing in from perfumes alone, Beckham's business success offers another glimpse into the commercial power he has built beyond football.David Beckham's fragrance business brings in over $23,000 dailyBeckham's perfume collection has become a significant part of his commercial portfolio. The range includes popular names such as Instinct, Classic Blue, True Instinct, Bold Instinct and Classic Homme. Unlike some celebrity-backed luxury products, his fragrances target a wider audience, with prices ranging from $16 to $66.The affordable pricing has not stopped the business from generating impressive returns. Its latest reported accounts showed $8.3 million in annual turnover and more than $7 million in profit. That puts its average daily revenue at roughly $22,740, or more than $23,000 when rounded.The company also reportedly holds $10.5 million in cash, while its assets are valued at approximately $13.8 million.The fragrance operation sits under Seven Global LLP, established in 2015 as a joint venture involving Beckham and Global Brands Group. His DB Ventures business took control of the company in 2022, expanding his influence over the products carrying his name.The figures show how Beckham has turned his international popularity into a profitable licensing operation. His name continues to sell even without the weekly excitement of a football match.Inter Miami and other investments add to David Beckham's billion-dollar fortunePerfumes are only one part of Beckham's growing business empire. His investments span sports, fashion, entertainment and wellness, giving him several sources of income beyond fragrance sales.One of his biggest ventures is Inter Miami CF, the MLS club he co-owns. Forbes valued the franchise at approximately $1.35 billion in 2026. Beckham reportedly owns a 26% stake, making the club a major part of his business portfolio.Lionel Messi's arrival has also helped elevate Inter Miami's global profile. The club has gained greater international attention, strengthening the value of Beckham's investment.His endorsement portfolio includes major brands such as Adidas, Armani and Gillette. He has also expanded into entertainment through production company Studio 99 and wellness through investments such as supplement brand IM8.Forbes estimated Beckham's personal net worth at $1 billion in 2026. His football career reportedly generated around $800 million in total earnings, including salaries, sponsorships and endorsements. His playing wages alone accounted for an estimated $125 million to $175 million before tax.Beckham retired from professional football in 2013 after a career that included 729 club appearances and 129 goals. Yet his earning power has continued to grow.His latest fragrance figures underline an important part of that success: Beckham has built a business identity that stands firmly on its own, even years after his final appearance on the pitch.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Fantasy Football Booms & Busts: Another 'craziest week of the season' in Week 8
articles.summary: Fantasy football analyst Scott Pianowski examines some of the biggest winners and losers in a wild Week 8.
articles.body:
It's a weekly staple. A bunch of exciting peak-and-valley football gets played and someone exhales and declares it the craziest week of the season. I typically just laugh. The NFL is the ultimate snow globe league; chaos is the main ingredient. This stuff should never surprise anyone.

But maybe I need to drink the Kool-Aid for Week 8. The opening window on Sunday made me dizzy, too.

Someone out there could realistically have a starting lineup that includes Lamar Jackson, Zay Flowers, Tre Tucker and Omar Cooper Jr. They all scored zero points, and only Jackson (busted thumb) was knocked out by injury. To be fair, when Jackson and then Tyler Huntley got hurt for the Ravens, Flowers was essentially crossed off, too.

The Buccaneers won a football game despite Baker Mayfield going 0-for-3 on passes. Mayfield still earned a 39.6 rating for his troubles, better than Michael Penix Jr. on the other side (four picks, 125 passing yards, 12.0 rating). Drake London had one catch for eight yards.

Every Minnesota football game is a tax on offense. This week was no exception (the Lions won the game, 19-15). At least Jahmyr Gibbs was unstoppable (23-153-1), and Jameson Williams (a credible 4-70-1), T.J. Hockenson and Justin Jefferson applied some touchdown deodorant.

Did you need Jacoby Brissett at Dallas? He was benched, then watched Gardner Minshew dial up three touchdown passes. Counting on Jonathan Taylor at Jacksonville? Twenty-three rushing yards. Parker Washington on the other side? One catch. The Jaguars targeted the entire phone book (11 players in all), and nobody drew more than three. Good times.

Is Ashton Jeanty your guy? He's essentially been benched for Mike Washington Jr. On and on it goes.

How do we refresh the palate after all this silliness? Call up the Dead Zone running backs.

Tony Pollard was almost a punchline during draft season. You want that back-nine running back, on that lousy team? But Pollard seems to survive every year, no matter the surroundings — he did collect four straight 1,000-yard rushing seasons before this year. And although his first quarter this year was slow off the mark, he does get decent volume every week. And the last two games, he's been shredding.

It started with 25-129-3 against Cleveland last week, and then continued with 137 total yards and two scores Sunday at Cincinnati. Ohio can't get past Pollard quick enough. It's also encouraging to see Pollard stepping into a receiving role with Tyjae Spears hurt; Pollard has six catches over the last two games. It's a shame his bye comes in Week 9 and the upcoming schedule is rough, but show Pollard some respect. Heck, maybe he'll work his way into NFL trade discussions; despite Pollard's surge, the one-win Titans are still going nowhere.

For most of the year we've talked about Jaylen Warren as a better real-life player than fantasy player. The lack of touchdowns has held him back, no fault of his own. But Warren merged the two streets nicely in the romp over Cleveland, darting and weaving for 143 rushing yards and his second rushing touchdown of the year. Of course the Steelers keep Rico Dowdle in the mix too (15-56-1), so that puts a cap on the Warren ceiling. But sometimes you just have to bet on talent. Warren and the Steelers take their bye in Week 9.

Remember when Bhayshul Tuten and Chris Rodriguez Jr. were in a quasi-job battle? Ah, summer is a blur now. Tuten has left Rodriguez in the dust, and finally Tuten is starting to get some touchdown luck, too (he's had multiple scores wiped out by penalty in 2026). Tuten threw 104 land yards at the Colts, 55 by air and scored a touchdown in both manners. Prices out at 28.9 points in half-point PPR scoring, good enough for the RB yellow jersey as we go to press. Baltimore is up next, the same defense that just got thumped in Buffalo.

Bucky Irving was the unwanted man in Tampa Bay this year, so the story went. Kenneth Gainwell signed a decent contract. Sean Tucker was around as a talented No. 3. But Irving has turned into one of the value picks of the year, getting his running groove back and surging behind what's all of a sudden a perfect setup in Tampa Bay. The Buccaneers' offensive line has been demolishing people of late. Baker Mayfield was 0-for-3 passing Sunday — OH FOR THREE — and threw for just 64 yards last week. Irving was so dominant in the dodgy weather against Atlanta (27-100-1) that he left some understudy work for Gainwell (25-140-0). It's like the Buccaneers went into a 1977 time machine and never came back. The Bears will be a fascinating matchup next Sunday night.

So what if Joe Burrow wants to do all of his term papers at the last minute? They all read like Shakespeare. The Bengals had a scoreless half last week before smashing Baltimore, and Sunday it was a sluggish first quarter before Burrow caught fire against Tennessee. The end result was 462 passing yards and five touchdowns, plus another score on the ground.

You'll excuse the three picks when the other columns are packed so thickly, and Burrow was kind enough to get a touchdown to all his main pass-catchers (Tee Higgins 10-155-2, Ja'Marr Chase 11-141-1, Mike Gesicki 4-76-1). Chase Brown? He had a modest 12-55-0 on the ground, but at least he scammed 8-46-0 in the passing game. And Samaje Perine wasn't in his way — just five touches for 19 yards. The Bengals and Falcons wing over to Spain next week.

Maybe it's unfair to call Mike Washington Jr. a boom — he had a modest 83 yards on 25 carries. But volume is a currency in fantasy football, and he received that workload while Jeanty was limited to two rushes for nine yards. Jeanty did snag three catches for 64 yards, but the Raiders won the game and Washington has been the better runner all year. Klint Kubiak teased changes all week, then brought some on game day. The Raiders are at San Francisco next.

Tyler Allgeier became the last Arizona back standing when Jeremiyah Love (ankle) and Bam Knight (concussion) were ruled out. No problem. Allgeier went bonkers at Dallas, racking up 191 total yards and two touchdowns. Before we get too excited about the Allgeier future, the upcoming schedule looks nasty (Seahawks, Rams, Chiefs). Maybe this is the week you throw him into a fantasy trade to land something bigger.

With Jackson needing thumb surgery and headed for injured reserve — that's at least four weeks down, perhaps the season — you have to wonder if the Ravens are cooked. If only the Bengals would let Baltimore have Joe Flacco back. Flowers drew five targets at Buffalo but they all fell incomplete. Derrick Henry (11-53-1) fell into the end zone to save his day, but the Ravens might want to take calls on Henry as the trade deadline approaches. With Jackson out and Huntley in limbo, the 4-4 Ravens could be drawing dead for 2026.

If you told me Cooper's bagel (zero catches, zero targets) came at the expense of Garrett Wilson bouncing back, I'd believe it. Well, Wilson had a solid but not seismic 6-83-0. It wasn't Mason Taylor, either — he was held to 3-19-0 on five targets. The big winner in the New York passing game was Adonai Mitchell, finally healthy again and smashing for 7-142-1 on nine targets. Just what the Jets need: a widening passing tree. At least we can set our watch by Braelon Allen (21-147-1), who is a monster every week. Breece Hall might have been Wally Pipp'ed in the Meadowlands.

The Colts were never competitive in Jacksonville and eventually it became open auditions for their next starting back (Taylor played 38 of 61 offensive snaps ). Seth McGowan had five rushes for 29 yards, and DJ Giddens locked up with a 6-43-0 log. Daniel Jones had another predictable lost game (5.1 YPA, 1 TD, 2 picks, 3 sacks), though he at least got a short touchdown to Josh Downs and some PPR scam to Keenan Allen (7-67-0). I'd stream almost any defense against the Colts, but not Dallas in Week 9.

articles.title: Fantasy Football Week 8 RB Report: Raiders relegate Ashton Jeanty to pure passing role, plus more on key backfield splits
articles.summary: In a wild Week 8 slate, we go over some backfield splits and what it all means for fantasy football.
articles.body:
What a way to come out of Halloween and right into November. If you had a fun weekend dressing up and celebrating, you were likely groaning a bit in the early part of the 1 p.m. ET Sunday window for fantasy football. But man, did things come alive in the second half of those games.

For the running back position, there's a lot to cover coming out of Week 8. There were plenty of surprising performances and injuries, which forced a shift in some key backfield splits. Let's get into it and what it all means for fantasy football going into Week 9.

The Raiders got by the Jets in a shootout at MetLife Stadium on Sunday afternoon, the total reaching 71 points. Las Vegas' passing game did most of the heavy lifting, but the RB split was eye-opening to say the least. Washington hadn't seen double-digit carries in any game so far this season. He got a career-high 25 in the victory, averaging 3.3 yards per carry. Jeanty barely got any ground work, relegated to strictly passing situations.

Washington didn't find the end zone, but that workload is what we're used to seeing for some of the top bell cow backs in the NFL. The rookie back is out there on the waiver wire in the majority of Yahoo leagues, so he needs to be on way more rosters after this game, regardless of production.

The big question is: Will this continue?

If it does, Jeanty is basically a receiver, so it'll be tough to trust him. He only saw four targets and we know Kirk Cousins is going to favor Brock Bowers in the passing game. Jeanty was trending toward a miserable week until a 45-yard catch on a screen.

If this is the case moving forward, Washington will become a viable fantasy RB3/flex option occupying the ground and goal line. Jeanty may be more involved in the run game in future weeks, but he appears to have the receiving role. While that's valuable, it could limit his snaps/carries. We need to see what the usage looks like in Week 9, but Jeanty is no longer a reliable RB2/3. He's more of a risky option with upside in PPR formats.

This was supposed to be the week. The week we saw Brown pop off. And when you look at the score of the Bengals-Titans OT game, a 43-36 victory for Cincy, you'd think that would mean a big day for Brown. But it was more of the same: an empty feeling for fantasy managers.

Brown got the volume again, reaching 20 or more touches for the fourth time this season. The Bengals scored six touchdowns but none went to the ground game, other than a Joe Burrow nine-yard rush to win the game. A lot of that we can chalk up to bad luck in a way. Four of Burrow's five TDs came from 17 yards or further out, the one outlier a Jack Endries goal-line TD. So while Brown may not have had a ton of scoring chances, there's still a major issue: he failed to develop any big plays in a dream matchup against the Titans.

His long on the ground was 14 yards. His long through the air was nine yards. The big plays still aren't there. Brown also PPR-scammed his way to double-digit fantasy points, just the third time he's gone over that mark this season.

The one positive coming out of this game is that Perine didn't vulture a TD or much of a role. We had seen Perine score in the previous two games for Cincy. So my take is that Brown still possesses a strong floor for an RB2/3 option. But I don't know if/when we will see the ceiling. It could come; it may not. You'd think we'd get some positive TD regression. The Bengals have a few favorable RB matchups coming up (next week against Falcons, Week 12 against Saints).

Brown is still a viable play and may not be a bad buy-low target in a trade. The touches are there. We know this offense can move the ball. I think we eventually see Brown find the end zone more and maybe we get some explosive plays. But beware of a potential RB trade by the Bengals before the trade deadline.

The Vikings offense is bad. And you've got to think the franchise is questioning the move to trade J.J. McCarthy to the Giants. Kyler Murray doesn't look like the answer at QB and it's impacting everyone around him. I mean, it's bad when Justin Jefferson is ducking the media after a game. Anyway, let's focus on the running game — or lack thereof.

Murray was the leading rusher not listed above with four carries for 35 yards. Mason had the majority of the ground work and none in the passing game with Jones healthy. But neither back was particularly good despite having a pretty solid draw against the Lions, who entered the game allowing just under 100 rushing yards per game. Detroit's front line is tougher than its secondary, but that's exactly the problem when looking at Minnesota. If you can't exploit a bad secondary, you can't open up the run game.

Looking ahead, the Vikings get the Bills next week, which feels a lot like this matchup against the Lions. Buffalo's offense should test Minnesota's defense plenty. If Murray can't get the offense moving, the Vikings could fall behind, which means less Mason and more Jones. I'd put Jones ahead of Mason right now given the passing game role, which isn't even that prominent. But it elevates Jones' floor. Mason would need everything to work in his favor — game script, volume, touchdown equity — in order to get fantasy managers home.

Neither back feels very appealing for fantasy right now. But the floor is there if the script permits. The problem is this passing game is subpar, which could make it easier for opposing defenses to game plan. Both backs are in shaky-flex territory.

This backfield was in the fantasy spotlight going into Week 8. The Cardinals were starring down a great matchup with the Cowboys and got their prized rookie back from injury. And early on, it was Love who was getting most of the work. But he wasn't very effective and failed to convert at the goal line. Then, Love exited after aggravating his ankle injury.

Knight had been leading the way with Love out before Week 8. He exited after sustaining a concussion on a big hit and fumble Sunday. So that left it all up to Allgeier. And he pretty much put the team on his back.

The veteran back had one of the best games of his career, turning 16 touches into nearly 200 total yards and two scores. He caught the ball, he made big plays, he did everything we sort of thought he might do — and more — if Love were to miss any time. That wasn't the case the previous two games but Allgeier showed up in the right spot.

Now, you've got to think the Cardinals consider shelving Love given how his ankle has been. Knight likely goes into concussion protocol and could miss Week 9 against the Seahawks. Ahhh yes, Seattle. That's the only downside if you're grabbing Allgeier off the waiver wire or if you are considering playing him next week. It's a tough draw, but if Knight and Love are sidelined, Allgeier would still be a decent RB3/flex option given the type of volume he'd receive.

Long-term, Allgeier's outlook is pretty solid if the other backs can't get healthy. There are some tough matchups, but Allgeier would be active in the passing game, elevating his floor. He isn't a bad player to target via trade as well before your deadline if the price is right.

This sure did feel like a long time coming, the turning of the tide in the Denver backfield. Coleman was able to return from IR last week, leading the backfield with nine carries for 54 yards with a pair of catches for 15. That was with Dobbins stealing a TD and RJ Harvey healthy, catching a few passes for 54 yards and a score. This week, however, it was all Coleman.

With Harvey landing on IR, instead of keeping things a committee, the Broncos gave Coleman the keys and he ran with it, helping Denver come back and knock off the Chiefs 28-24. Coleman set up his winning score with a 51-yard catch-and-run. He's clearly the back with the most juice and we knew head coach Sean Payton liked him going into the season. Coleman just needed to get healthy. Now that he is, it looks like he's the back to roster on this team.

Coleman is in the RB2/3 range but it's closer to RB2. Even when Harvey returns, Payton should play the best back and that's clearly Coleman right now. Without the goal-line role, which Coleman dominated, Dobbins may find himself a drop candidate soon. We could see Harvey return and retain his pass-game role, while Coleman dominates the ground, but still runs routes given his talent.

articles.title: Kimi Antonelli becomes youngest champion in F1 history at age 20
articles.summary: Twenty-year-old Mercedes driver Kimi Antonelli has become the youngest champion in the history of Formula 1 with four races still left in the season.
articles.body: After crossing the finish line of the Mexico City Grand Prix behind race winner Max Verstappen and Lewis Hamilton, F1 history-maker Kimi Antonelli placed his hands on the steering wheel and his voice cracked as he said, “We did it, we did it.” Although the 20-year-old Mercedes driver finished third in the Mexican capital on Sunday, he became the youngest champion in the history of Formula 1. “Thank you so much, we did it, we did it, thank you so much … thank you,” Antonelli said on the team radio after securing the title with four races still left in the season. Antonelli, the first Italian to win the title since Alberto Ascari in 1953, took an unassailable lead in the standings over teammate George Russell and Ferrari’s Hamilton. Sebastian Vettel was the previous youngest champion at age 23 in 2010. Verstappen won the Mexico City GP for the sixth time. “I would not be here, without Mercedes and my family, I am speechless just trying to process this,” Antonelli said at the end of the race. “It has been an incredible season.” Italy’s joy “For 73 years, our country has waited for this moment, and today an entire nation will celebrate one of its own reaching the very pinnacle of our sport,” said Formula 1 CEO Stefano Domenicali. “Today, his name joins the legends of our sport. A new chapter in Formula 1 history has been written, and I firmly believe this is only the beginning of an extraordinary legacy.” Race stopped The race was stopped on lap 46 with a red flag after Valtteri Bottas crashed into the wall at the first corner, following issues with his right-side suspension. Cadillac reported that the driver was given “further medical assessments as a precaution.” Bottas had got out of the car unaided and waved to the fans before leaving the track. At the restart, Verstappen was first — followed by Charles Leclerc, Hamilton, Antonelli, Lando Norris and Russell — and the Red Bull driver did not let the win slip away. After Mexico, F1 will head to Brazil and then to Las Vegas. It remains uncertain whether the final two scheduled Grands Prix — in Qatar and Abu Dhabi —will take place, given instability in the region. Ferrari’s unhappy teammates Hamilton, who had secured pole position on Saturday, lost it on the fourth lap while battling for the lead with Leclerc. Hamilton briefly went off track, dropping back to third place. The maneuver between the two Ferrari drivers was investigated, resulting in a five-second penalty for Leclerc — a decision that left seven-time world champion Hamilton fuming. “The stewards are basically handing Charles this win. We agreed in the drivers’ briefing,” Hamilton said. “The problem with a 5-second penalty is that he’s got clean air and doesn’t have to manage (the car) like the rest of us. He should have just given the position back.” Shortly before the red flag caused by Bottas’ crash, Hamilton radioed, “We’ve got problems … big, big problems.” On pulling into the garage, he appeared visibly frustrated with his team. Aston Martin’s troubles After a disastrous qualifying, Fernando Alonso joked that he wouldn’t race in Mexico and would head straight to Brazil instead. That nearly became a reality. Alonso, a two-time F1 champion, was forced to retire early, with his teammate Lance Stroll exiting the race shortly afterward on the seventh lap, capping off a disastrous visit to Mexico for the Aston Martin team. “I was just told to retire the car due to an engine issue. I’m not sure what happened. The car was fine during the first practice sessions, then it failed in qualifying, and now it’s happened again,” Alonso said. “We had reliability issues at the worst possible time.”

articles.title: Lessons from Prakash fuel Tirthank Pegu’s Youth Olympics push
articles.summary: KOLKATA: As Tirthank Pegu prepares for the biggest competition of his young career, his biggest takeaway from the last few months has little to do with
articles.body: KOLKATA: As Tirthank Pegu prepares for the biggest competition of his young career, his biggest takeaway from the last few months has little to do with lap times or race strategies.The Assam swimmer, who will represent India in the 100m and 200m butterfly at Youth Olympics in Dakar, Senegal, spent six weeks training in Europe, including a stint alongside India’s most accomplished butterfly swimmer, Sajan Prakash. While the sessions in Spain and Scotland helped sharpen his technique, Pegu says the lessons he learnt outside the pool could prove just as valuable.“My target was to go sub-two minutes in the 200m butterfly because Sajan Prakash is the only Indian swimmer who has achieved that. Training with him taught me a lot, not only about the event itself but also about life beyond swimming,” Pegu told STOI.Fresh from a personal-best performance at Singapore National Age Group Swimming Championships in March, where he clocked 2:00.96 in the 200m butterfly to grab bronze after improving from his previous best of 2:02.56, Pegu travelled to Spain for a three-week high-altitude camp before heading directly to Scotland for another three weeks of preparation.The Singapore meet, however, proved to be a turning point.“It gave me a huge mental boost. Dropping two seconds in an event like the 200m butterfly made me more confident in myself and in my coach’s training,” said the 18-year-old.That confidence only grew during his European camps, where he had the opportunity to observe first-hand how elite swimmers approach their craft.According to Pegu, one of the most important lessons from Prakash was understanding that success in swimming is built away from the pool as much as inside it.“He taught me that swimming is not only about training in the water. It’s about your lifestyle, the habits you maintain and the discipline you follow every day. The way you live your life shows up in the pool,” said Pegu during a virtual interaction from Dakar on Saturday.The youngster believes those conversations helped strengthen him mentally as he chases one of the biggest goals of his career. While qualifying for the Youth Olympics fulfilled a dream he shared with his father, Pegu has also developed a larger purpose.“When I was training in Delhi, there were times when I felt negative. A lot of people still don’t believe that Indian swimmers can achieve great results at major international events like the Asian Games or the Commonwealth Games,” said Pegu, who currently trains at Inspire Institute of Sport in Vijayanagar, Karnataka.The 18-year-old hopes strong performances by Indian swimmers on the global stage can change those perceptions. “My goal is to help Indian swimming reach a level where people take us seriously and support us more,” he added.For now, however, his complete focus remains on the Youth Olympics, and the 100m and 200m butterfly events he will compete in.Armed with confidence from a breakthrough year, six weeks of training in Europe and lessons learned from veteran Prakash, Pegu hopes to turn those experiences into a medal-winning performance on the biggest stage of his junior career.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Kimi Antonelli becomes Formula One’s youngest world champion in Mexico City
articles.summary: Italian wonderkid wins drivers’ championship at 20 years and 68 days, finishing third at the Mexico City Grand Prix.
articles.body:
⁠Kimi Antonelli has become Formula One’s youngest world champion ⁠at 20 years and 68 days old with his third-place finish for Mercedes at the Mexico City Grand Prix.

The first Italian champion since 1953 sobbed with joy over the team radio as he took the chequered flag at the high-altitude Autodromo Hermanos Rodriguez on Sunday.

Red Bull’s Max Verstappen won the red-flagged, restarted race for his second win of the season, but Antonelli’s overall lead ⁠reached an unassailable 119 points after finishing third.

Ferrari’s Lewis Hamilton started from pole position and took a close second place – after clashing with teammate Charles Leclerc – on an afternoon of drama, with two safety cars, multiple crashes and an agonising 33-minute halt with 25 of the 71 laps remaining.

“Get in there, Kimi. Champion of the world,” said his race engineer Peter Bonnington, a regular target for the young driver’s practical jokes.

“We did it. Thank you so much,” ⁠gasped the Italian, whose parents and sister were there to embrace him when he stepped out of the car. He was then mobbed by his pit crew.

The previous youngest champion was Germany’s Sebastian Vettel, who took the first of his four with Red Bull at 23 years and 134 days old in 2010.

“I’m speechless. I’m trying to process what has just happened,” Antonelli said to the crowd.

“It’s been an incredible season, and to share this podium with Max and Lewis is truly incredible. And looking forward to some more battles in the future.

“This weekend, I did feel a bit more tense, but I’m just so happy that we got it done, and now ‌we can enjoy the rest of the season,” he added, as he stood on the podium with an Italian flag wrapped around his shoulders, spraying the champagne with abandon.

The last Italian champion was Alberto Ascari, 73 years earlier.

“On the last lap, I just backed off, because I just couldn’t see the track. I was getting emotional,” Antonelli told a later news conference.

Leclerc finished fourth, McLaren’s outgoing champion Lando Norris fifth, and Antonelli’s teammate George Russell only sixth in a race he had to win to have any chance of staying in contention.

That also meant that Verstappen went second in the overall standings, with Hamilton third and preseason favourite Russell plummeting to fourth, 130 points behind Antonelli.

Mercedes have 630 points in the constructors’ standings to Ferrari’s 504 and could clinch that title in Brazil next weekend.

The race was stopped after a brief safety car deployment on lap 46 of 71 after Valtteri Bottas suffered a high-speed front-left suspension failure down the straight, with his Cadillac pitching uncontrollably into the barriers at turn one.

Bottas received medical attention in the car, but then walked to an ambulance, giving a thumbs-⁠up, as the rest of the field returned to the pits. He went to the medical centre and was released.

Verstappen led from the restart, challenged by Hamilton, with Antonelli passing Leclerc. There was then another safety car when Lindblad and Piastri collided, with the field released to race again with nine laps to the ⁠chequered flag.

Hamilton had led away from the original pole position for the 105th time in his career, but the first for Ferrari at a full Grand Prix, with Leclerc slotting in behind from third on the grid.

The British driver held him off as they went side by side through the opening corners, but Leclerc cut turn four and went across the grass as they battled for the lead, with Verstappen then taking second from Hamilton as the Ferrari looped wide.

“Pushed out by ‌my own teammate,” Hamilton said over the radio.

The stewards handed Leclerc a five-second penalty, but that did little for Hamilton, who remained behind his teammate after their respective stops on laps 28 and 29, with the Monegasque taking his penalty.

Russell, who had lined up on the front row, made a poor start and dropped to fifth. He also collided with Hadjar, punting the Red Bull off, and the stewards handed him a 10-second penalty.

articles.title: Philadelphia Eagles lose sixth straight as Washington Commanders score 27 unanswered points
articles.summary: Tanner McKee's turnovers and a costly illegal formation penalty doomed the Philadelphia Eagles as Washington scored 27 unanswered points Sunday.
articles.body: The Philadelphia Eagles are in free-fall. After building an early 10-0 lead, Philadelphia gave up 27 unanswered points in a 27-10 loss to the Washington Commanders on Sunday Night Football. Philadelphia started fast. Jake Elliott hit a 40-yard field goal, and Saquon Barkley scored on a three-yard run after a Washington turnover. The Eagles never scored again. Washington took over behind Jayden Daniels and kicker Drew Stevens. Stevens hit a 56-yard field goal late in the first quarter, Daniels found Stefon Diggs for an eight-yard score in the second, and Stevens added a 39-yard kick before halftime to put Washington up 13-10. JALEN HURTS TO REPORTEDLY MISS REMAINDER OF NFL SEASON AFTER BLOOD CLOTS FOUND IN QUARTERBACK'S LUNGS Philadelphia has no answers without Jalen Hurts. Tanner McKee looked like a backup all night, holding the ball, taking sacks, refusing to throw downfield and turning the ball over twice. Without Hurts, Washington stacked the box and held Barkley to 30 yards on 13 carries. The turning point came in the third quarter. Dorance Armstrong strip-sacked McKee, and Charles Omenihu recovered the fumble. Daniels hit Treylon Burks for 53 yards on the next play, setting up a 25-yard Stevens kick. When Philadelphia finally drove into scoring position in the fourth quarter, mental mistakes wiped it out. Elliott made an apparent 36-yard field goal to cut the deficit to three, but an illegal formation penalty on left tackle Jordan Mailata took the points off the board. Backed up five yards, Elliott missed wide right. Washington closed it out. Stevens kicked a 42-yard field goal with 3:43 left. Commanders cornerback Rasul Douglas intercepted McKee on the next possession. Rachaad White broke off a 33-yard run and scored from a yard out with 1:52 remaining, and Austin Ekeler ran in a two-point conversion to make it 27-10. Daniels finished with 217 passing yards, one touchdown and no turnovers. Philadelphia has lost six straight games, falling to 2-6. Washington improves to 2-4-1, climbing out of last place in the NFC East. articles.title: ‘21-day non-entry rule’: Why Asa Tribe has been barred from joining England Lions in West Indies
articles.summary: Asa Tribe has been ruled out of the England Lions' West Indies tour due to a 21-day non-entry rule.
articles.body:
Asa Tribe has been barred from joining England Lions in West Indies due to a 21-day travel restriction in Saint Kitts & Nevis.

The Glamorgan batter recently represented Jersey in ICC Cricket World Cup Challenge League in Nairobi, Kenya.

The restriction is linked to Ebola concerns in Kenya and other African countries.

Tribe has returned to the UK, with the ECB liaising with authorities.

Why has Asa Tribe been barred from joining England Lions in West Indies?

Glamorgan batter Asa Tribe is set to be unavailable for England Lions' white-ball series against West Indies A due to being barred from entering Saint Kitts & Nevis following his recent trip to Kenya.

The 22-year-old was picked in both T20 and ODI squads but will miss out on traveling to the Caribbean country after falling under their 21-day ban imposed for individuals who visited countries with cases of Ebola fears.

This follows an appearance by Tribe for Jersey in ICC Cricket World Cup Challenge League held in Nairobi, Kenya in October.

Why does the 21-day non-entry rule apply?

This Government of Saint Kitts & Nevis imposed the restriction due to apprehensions regarding the Ebola virus infection in some regions of Africa.

As per its October 15 travel advisory , non-citizens who have been to any one of six specified high-risk nations within 21 days prior to their arrival will not be permitted entry into the nation.

The restriction also covers passengers that do not belong to the nation and have made a transit journey through any of these countries regardless of their having left the airport premises.

The advisory will be in force until such a time when the authorities decide on changing the advisories.

What has the ECB said about Asa Tribe's absence?

The England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) confirmed that Tribe had already returned to the UK after the entry ban.

"Saint Kitts & Nevis currently have a 21-day non-entry rule in place for non-nationals who have been in Kenya due to the Ebola situation in Kenya and seven other countries in Africa," an ECB spokesman said to BBC Sport Wales .

"Asa is back in the UK, and we are in touch with the relevant authorities," the spokesperson added.

Tribe's absence has nothing to do with the virus; there has not been any report about him contracting or being a suspected patient of the virus.

How has Asa Tribe performed for Glamorgan?

Tribe had a good 2026 season with Glamorgan. He amassed 940 runs, averaging 37.60, including two centuries in 14 County Championship games.

Additionally, he has left a mark in England Lions' games, with 129 not out against Australia A in Brisbane in December 2025, followed by 135 against South Africa A in May 2026.

Although Tribe has played international games representing Jersey, he is still eligible to play for England since his country is an ICC full member and Jersey is an associate member.

Tribe has been quoted talking about his desire to represent England senior team, and he has also been negotiating with England managing director Rob Key.

articles.title: Mike Washington Jr. steals most of the rushing work in Vegas in Week 8
articles.summary: Mike Washington Jr. handled 25 of the Raiders' 28 carries by running backs in Week 8 but could only turn them into 83 yards against the Jets.
articles.body:
Las Vegas Raiders RB Mike Washington Jr. carried 25 times for 83 yards in a Week 8 win over the New York Jets.

Why It Matters: The rookie entered with just 40 carries on the season to go with a 4.9 yards per attempt average, so this comes as a bit of a surprise even though Ashton Jeanty has struggled to run the ball efficiently this season. Based on head coach Klint Kubiak's postgame comments, it appears Washington will continue to factor very heavily into the running game plans moving forward while Jeanty handles most of the work in the passing game. As such, Washington should be considered a RB3/flex option for Week 9 against the 49ers - albeit a low-end one.

articles.title: “Was Not Dirty”: Ex-Browns Player Defends Mason McCormick for Body Slamming Jared Verse in Steelers’ Win vs. Browns
articles.summary: Until the Week 8 Browns-Steelers clash, Jared Verse only felt the rivalry as a teammate. He’d been hyping the game up, trash-talking Pittsburgh before.
articles.body:
Until the Week 8 Browns-Steelers clash, Jared Verse only felt the rivalry as a teammate. He'd been hyping the game up, trash-talking Pittsburgh before. But during the game, the rivalry became personal for him.

On an extra point attempt by the Steelers, offensive lineman Mason McCormick tossed (an already airborne) Verse headfirst into the ground. This became a highlight of the game and fed into the rivalry. But according to former Cleveland player Jason Pinkston, McCormick did nothing wrong.

"Browns fans… I love y'all, but what Mason McCormick did to Jared Verse was NOT dirty at all! As an offensive lineman, you're taught from day one that if a defensive player leaves his feet and jumps, YOU DUMP HIM! That's Offensive Line 101," wrote Pinkston on X .

McCormick said the same thing after the game:

"I really had no idea who it was. Just felt somebody jump, and we're told to get jumpers' hands down."

He never implied that the move was personally motivated because of everything Verse has said about the Steelers so far. It happened as a natural reaction. But he was still flagged for the move, with officials declaring it unnecessary roughness.

Verse came to Cleveland only this year by way of the Myles Garrett trade with the Los Angeles Rams. And in the short time that has passed since, he has gone real deep into the rivalry Cleveland has with Pittsburgh. In their earlier matchup this season, Verse said during the game, "I hate the black and yellow, man. I hate it."

Jared Verse had also accused the Steelers of playing "dirty," along with a bold claim later about "making Pittsburgh ours."

However, the defensive end couldn't match that fire in his game. Against the Steelers in Week 8, Jared Verse only recorded one assisted tackle.

He was also beyond unhappy with McCormick's play.

"I had jumped in the air, tried to block the kick, he swooped my legs in the air, ended up landing on my head," Verse said in the post-game presser. "That's football. I mean, I'm very upset about it. Obviously, you know, if this wasn't football, I would have reacted a different way. But, you know, he got to handle that. He got the flag, you know, he was able to walk away with it. He got a little penalty on them.

"I love how much power goes into it. How much we put into their lives, into the football. But to do something like that? It's just, I can't have respect for anything like that."

While Verse lost respect for Pittsburgh, Pinkston believes that it was not foul play from McCormick. It is a basic technique taught to offensive linemen from the beginning of their football careers.

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes admits to AFC West reality after Chiefs loss to Broncos

articles.body:
Patrick Mahomes flung a desperation pass hoping to squeeze some final heroics against the Denver Broncos . But the Kansas City Chiefs quarterback took a sack before firing the ball off, ending the game. And the conclusion of that dramatic 28-24 Broncos win forced Mahomes to admit a new, AFC West reality.

Mahomes got honest with reporters after the game about the new state of the division.

"Obviously, it was a big game. I mean, I'm not gonna hide from that, but now you're kinda in a dogfight for the division," Mahomes said.

Kansas City became spoiled with one division title after another in the era of Andy Reid and Mahomes. The franchise collected nine straight division crowns until 2025 arrived .

That injury ravaged Chiefs team succumbed to a 6-11 record, snapping their impressive streak of claiming the AFC West. But who leapfrogged them and everyone else? Sunday's victors inside Empower Field.

Then the huge Thanksgiving showdown against the Buffalo Bills. But the Chiefs are now navigating in an AFC West that features three teams above .500.

articles.title: Makai Lemon squeezes team-high 57 yards out of six catches
articles.summary: Makai Lemon led the Eagles in targets (9), receptions (6), and receiving yards (57) in a Week 8 loss to Washington.
articles.body:
Philadelphia Eagles WR Makai Lemon had six receptions for 57 yards versus the Washington Commanders in Week 8. Lemon was targeted a game-high nine times.

Why It Matters: Faced with another night of not having DeVonta Smith (hamstring) or Dontayvion Wicks (ankle), Tanner McKee looked to the team's first-round pick nine times on Sunday night. The rookie responded with six catches for 57 yards. It's middling production to be sure, but it's getting Lemon some much-needed reps after he was almost invisible over the first six games of 2026. While it's unclear how much he'll be featured once Smith and/or Wicks return, Lemon is worth owning as a WR4/WR5 type that should at least offer flex value for as long as he remains the de facto lead receiver.

articles.title: Yankees Coach On The Verge Of Landing With Rival Club After World Series
articles.summary: The New York Yankees are in offseason mode following their disappointing loss in the postseason to the eventual American League champion Tampa Bay Rays.While...
articles.body:
The New York Yankees are in offseason mode following their disappointing loss in the postseason to the eventual American League champion Tampa Bay Rays.

While next year's Yankees roster won't look the same as the roster that helped deliver 93 wins in 2026, one figure who has already been confirmed to return for 2027 is manager Aaron Boone, despite objections from the fans.

However, one member of the coaching staff who appears to be on the verge of departure is bench coach Brad Ausmus, who is being connected to a rival club once more.

New York Yankees Bench Coach Brad Ausmus Reportedly On The Verge Of Landing With AL Rival

Based on a report that emerged this weekend, Ausmus could be on the verge of joining a bitter American League rival of the Yankees.

According to Astros beat writer Brian McTaggart, Ausmus has interviewed for a position with the Houston Astros , a club that he's already interviewed with for previous positions in the past.

"Brad Ausmus was in the Astros offices on Thursday, multiple people tell told MLB .com. He has previously interviewed for GM and manager positions in years past," McTaggart wrote on X, formerly known as Twitter.

The Astros did not retain manager Joe Espada, who had been in his position since the start of the 2024 campaign; they were defeated in a quick two-game sweep in the American League Wild Card playoff round by the Chicago White Sox .

Brad Ausmus Has Been With The Yankees Since 2023

Ausmus, who was hired by the Yankees in 2023, joined the San Diego Padres as a field executive in 2011 before becoming manager of the Detroit Tigers in 2013.

He led Detroit to an AL Central title and a 90-72 record in his first season, but the Tigers were swept by Baltimore in the Division Series. After a 74-87 season in 2015, Detroit rebounded to 86-75 in 2016.

The Tigers then lost 98 games in 2017 and parted ways with Ausmus, who finished his four-year tenure with a 314-332 record. Ausmus later managed the Los Angeles Angels for one season in 2019, going 72-90, before serving as the Oakland Athletics' bench coach in 2022.

articles.title: Padres Face $23.15 Million Decision on All-Star as Key Deadline Nears
articles.summary: The Padres face a Nov. 2 qualifying-offer decision on Adrian Morejon. Here’s what a $23.15 million commitment could mean for their bullpen. The post Padres F...
articles.body:
The San Diego Padres have another important deadline approaching, and this decision could affect both their bullpen and their future draft capital. Adrian Morejon is eligible for a qualifying offer, a one-year contract worth $23.15 million this offseason, according to The Associated Press. San Diego must decide whether to make that commitment before the November 2 deadline.

MLB.com's Sunday Padres report identifies the cutoff as 2 p.m. Pacific, or 4 p.m. Central. San Diego had not announced a qualifying offer at the time of this report. Only 18 of 157 qualifying offers have been accepted since the system began, the AP reported. That history provides context, but San Diego still must budget for the possibility of acceptance.

The question now goes beyond whether the Padres want Morejon back. They must decide whether preserving the possibility of draft compensation is worth the chance that he accepts an expensive one-year agreement. For a team with multiple pitching needs, that distinction deserves attention before the deadline arrives.

Adrian Morejon's Value Goes Beyond His Save Total

Baseball Savant's season record shows Morejon finished 2026 with a 2.83 ERA, 107 strikeouts and a 1.08 WHIP across 86 innings. He appeared in 76 games and recorded three saves. Those numbers describe a substantial workload without the closer label. His value came from handling important outs throughout the season, giving San Diego another trusted option around its ninth-inning plans.

The left-hander also struck out 107 hitters while walking 28. That combination helps explain why his market should involve more than teams simply looking to fill a traditional closing vacancy. However, a qualifying offer requires the Padres to prepare for an actual commitment. They cannot reasonably treat acceptance as impossible because another team might eventually offer more years.

Morejon would control that response if San Diego extends the offer. His next contract could therefore involve a choice between immediate guaranteed money and the opportunity to pursue a longer agreement.

The Qualifying Offer Creates Two Different Outcomes

If Morejon accepts, the Padres retain him on the one-year contract. Should he reject the offer and sign elsewhere, San Diego can receive draft compensation under the qualifying-offer rules. Gaslamp Ball's qualifying-offer explainer outlined that tradeoff earlier this offseason. The approaching deadline now turns that discussion into an immediate roster decision.

Rejection would not prevent the Padres from continuing to negotiate with Morejon. Likewise, extending the offer would not establish that a multiyear agreement is close. MLB.com predicts an offer and a rejection , but that remains a forecast.

The practical question is whether San Diego would be comfortable with either outcome. Draft compensation provides value if he leaves, while acceptance would preserve a productive pitcher at a meaningful cost. The compensation is a draft asset, not a replacement pitcher. San Diego would still need to acquire the innings and matchup value that Morejon supplied, making the two outcomes materially different roster paths. The deadline will show how the Padres balance those possibilities.

articles.title: Mets flex Nolan McLean’s Gold Glove award with awesome message
articles.summary: The New York Mets did not hold back in celebrating Nolan McLean’s latest accomplishment. McLean won the 2026 National League Gold Glove Award for pitchers o...
articles.body:
The New York Mets did not hold back in celebrating Nolan McLean 's latest accomplishment. McLean won the 2026 National League Gold Glove Award for pitchers on Sunday, and the Mets marked the occasion with a fitting message on social media.

"Nolan is Golden! Nolan McLean has won the Gold Glove for National League Pitchers!" the team wrote on X .

It is the first Gold Glove of McLean's young career, and it caps an impressive first full season in the majors for the right-hander. McLean beat out fellow finalists Michael McGreevy of the St. Louis Cardinals and Chris Sale of the Atlanta Braves to take home the honor.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

McLean ranked third among NL pitchers in defensive runs saved this season, trailing only McGreevy and Shota Imanaga of the Chicago Cubs. Gold Glove winners are determined by a combination of manager and coach voting, which accounts for 75% of the decision, and a statistical component that makes up the remaining 25%.

His glove work was only part of the story. McLean made 31 starts in 2026, going 12-10 with a 3.16 ERA, 194 strikeouts and a 1.17 WHIP across 179 2/3 innings. He entered the season as one of the top contenders for NL Rookie of the Year after posting a 5-1 record and a 2.06 ERA in eight starts following his debut in August 2025 , and he remained rookie-eligible heading into this year.

What McLean took the most pride in, though, was his reliability. With injuries hitting the Mets' rotation, he never missed a turn.

"I think the biggest thing is just not missing the start," McLean said in September. He added, "I try to take pride in going out there and competing every single time."

McLean was one of three Mets named Gold Glove finalists, along with catcher Luis Torrens and rookie right fielder Carson Benge. Torrens lost out to Gabriel Moreno of the Arizona Diamondbacks, while Benge fell short to Moreno's teammate Corbin Carroll.

The award is a bright spot in what was otherwise a frustrating year in Queens. The Mets fired manager Carlos Mendoza midseason after a 34-47 start before Andy Green took over, and they missed the playoffs for the second straight season .

Still, McLean's emergence gives the Mets plenty to build around heading into 2027. If he continues to develop at this rate, more hardware could be in his future.

articles.title: Oilers star Connor McDavid needed just 50 seconds to score highlight goal vs. Rangers
articles.summary: Edmonton Oilers center Connor McDavid needed just 50 seconds to steal the spotlight with another stunning finish in Sunday night’s 4-1 win over the New York...
articles.body:
Edmonton Oilers center Connor McDavid needed just 50 seconds to steal the spotlight with another stunning finish in Sunday night's 4-1 win over the New York Rangers at Madison Square Garden. The victory extended Edmonton's winning streak to three games and kept its perfect road record intact at 7-0-0.

McDavid opened the scoring with an impressive individual effort on his first shift. After receiving a short pass from Evan Bouchard in the neutral zone, the Oilers captain bounced the puck off the boards to himself before accelerating into the offensive zone. He then raced past Rangers defenseman Vladislav Gavrikov, cut toward the net and lifted the puck over rookie goaltender Dylan Garand.

The goal was McDavid's ninth of the season and his eighth career opening-minute strike, moving him past Mark Messier for the most in franchise history. It was also the 418th goal of his NHL career, putting him ahead of Glenn Anderson for sole possession of fourth place on Edmonton's all-time scoring list.

McDavid also provided an assist on Bouchard's second-period power-play goal, stretching his season-opening assist streak to 15 games. He also reached 30 assists faster than anyone in the history of the league, surpassing Wayne Gretzky's previous record of 16 games, set during the 1984-85 season.

The 29-year-old finished the contest with 39 points and extended his season-opening point streak to 15 games for the second time in his career. He previously recorded a 17-game run to begin the 2021-22 campaign.

Forward Colton Dach also played a major role in the win, scoring twice. His first goal arrived at 6:19 of the opening period to make it 2-0, while his empty-netter with 40 seconds remaining completed the scoring.

Bouchard contributed one goal and two assists, reaching 26 points through 15 games. That achievement places him among just four defensemen in NHL history to record at least 25 points over their first 15 games of a season, joining Bobby Orr, Al MacInnis and Denis Potvin.

Meanwhile, netminder Matt Tomkins made 27 saves in his first big-league appearance since April 17, 2024, earning his fourth career victory. Pavel Dorofeyev scored New York's only goal, while Garand stopped 21 shots.

The defeat was the Rangers' fourth consecutive loss and their sixth in seven games. They also continued a troubling pattern of conceding the opening goal in each of their four straight defeats.

The Oilers will attempt to continue their winning run when they visit the New Jersey Devils on Tuesday night.

articles.title: ‘Weakest call I have ever seen’: Brittany Mahomes criticizes referees after Chiefs’ loss to Broncos
articles.summary: The Kansas City Chiefs appeared to have pulled off a dramatic last-second win over the Denver Broncos on Sunday, when Patrick Mahomes found Rashee Rice for a...
articles.body:
The Kansas City Chiefs appeared to have pulled off a dramatic last-second win over the Denver Broncos on Sunday, when Patrick Mahomes found Rashee Rice for a go-ahead touchdown as time expired. Unfortunately for the Chiefs, a false start penalty wiped the score off the board, and the Broncos held on for a 28-24 victory.

Needless to say, Mahomes' wife Brittany was not happy with the call, and she made that clear on social media after the game as she absolutely blasted the referees.

The Chiefs seemed to be on their way to a win in Denver on Sunday afternoon. Unfortunately, that's not how it worked out.

Kansas City had squandered a 24-13 fourth-quarter lead, as Denver scored 15 unanswered points to take a 28-24 lead. The Chiefs mounted a comeback of their own and seemed to score a go-ahead touchdown, but it ultimately didn't count.

Mahomes then drove the Chiefs from their own 44 to the Denver 1-yard line, where he hit Rice for what looked like the game-winner. However, officials flagged right tackle Jaylon Moore for a false start, nullifying the score and moving Kansas City back to the 6. On the ensuing fourth down, Malcolm Roach sacked Mahomes to end the game.

Replays showed Moore's hip move slightly as he glanced toward Mahomes, but Chiefs head coach Andy Reid wasn't convinced it was a penalty.

"I didn't see it," Reid said in his postgame press conference, via Yahoo Sports . "That's one man's opinion. I saw him move his head, but I didn't see a false start."

Shortly after the game, Brittany Mahomes took to Instagram to share her frustration with the referees.

"You can't tell me you call that on a game winning TD, oh wait yeah I can cause it's us," Brittany wrote in a post on Instagram that was quickly picked up by Jomboy Media .. "That was the weakest call I have ever seen, you can't tell me otherwise."

Clearly, she was not at all happy with the decision.

articles.title: Tre Tucker pulls a disappearing act in Week 8 shootout

Las Vegas Raiders WR Tre Tucker had no receptions and just one target in a Week 8 win over the New York Jets.
