articles.title: Predators Buy Low on Shane Wright in Trade with Kraken
articles.summary: The Nashville Predators bought low on Shane Wright, hoping that this deal would be one of those that pay off big time. The post Predators Buy Low on Shane Wr...
articles.body:
The Nashville Predators pulled off a bit of a surprising trade on Sunday, landing former fourth-overall pick Shane Wright from the Seattle Kraken.

The deal was a classic example of buying low. After months of speculation, the Kraken cut bait on Wright, a player the organization swore it would not sell low.

The deal wasn't that bad, as the Kraken got back another former first-rounder, Matthew Wood.

The Predators are trying to make the most of an opportunity. It was plainly evident that Wright never really got on in Seattle. He had two tough seasons in which the Kraken avoided burning the first year of his entry-level deal.

When the organization finally decided to give him a real shot, it seemed he had arrived. During the 2024-25 season, Wright scored 19 goals and 44 points. Those totals, however, seem like a mirage. He slumped the following year, leading to questions about his consistency.

This season, it seemed the Kraken had enough. The 22-year-old has three goals and four points in 14 games.

While his offensive numbers haven't been atrocious, Shane Wright's overall game hasn't been commensurate with his draft status. And it's that situation that prompted the team to seek a trade. The Kraken were hoping that some other organization would put together a decent offer that would land them a top-six scorer. Alas, that wasn't exactly what the Predators did.

What Does Nashville Gain From Shane Wright Trade

So, what do the Predators gain from this Shane Wright trade?

On the surface, the Preds are taking on a reclamation project. GM Chris MacFarland is trying to bank on Wright's upside. He's still 22 and has plenty of runway to show that he can become a legit top-six forward in the NHL.

That situation may actually pan out by playing alongside consummate pros like Steven Stamkos and Ryan O'Reilly.

And O'Reilly may very well be the reason why the Predators made this move. The veteran center will be a UFA at the end of the season, and, well, it's uncertain whether O'Reilly will return to Nashville next season.

Now, it's far too soon to anoint Shane Wright as O'Reilly's successor. But at least his acquisition gives the Predators something to work with.

Ultimately, the NHL is a business. MacFarland understands that well. And if things work out well for Shane Wright in Nashville, the club could have a flippable asset at the deadline.

The Preds are teetering between a rebuild and contending. Thus far, Nashville has been one of those in-betweeners. But as the season wears on, it will become evident where they stand.

And if the Predators decide to sell, a successful and productive Shane Wright might just become an intriguing target for contending teams looking for some depth at the NHL trade deadline.

If anything, Wright might find his ceiling in Nashville, allowing him to dispel the concerns that came with his unceremonious slide in the 2022 NHL Draft.

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes Bracing For ‘Dogfight’ For AFC West After Broncos Loss
articles.summary: Kansas City Chiefs quarterback Patrick Mahomes spoke out on the team's loss to the Denver Broncos and the state of the AFC West. The post Patrick Mahomes Bra...
articles.body:
A late false start penalty on right tackle Jaylon Moore stripped the Kansas City Chiefs of a game-winning touchdown with just four seconds left on the clock in the game, down four points at home against division rivals, the Denver Broncos.

A sack on the final play of the game sealed the Chiefs' fate, and saw the Chiefs move to 5-2 on the season and surrender top position in the AFC West.

Having not won the division for the first in a decade last season, KC will no doubt be more cognizant than ever to not take divisional games for granted. Especially now that they lie second to Denver.

Mahomes Ready to Battle it Out For AFC West After Defeat

Speaking to the media after the game, Mahomes spoke about the state of the division half-way through the season, claiming that both them and the Broncos were in a "dogfight" for the division.

"Now, you're kind of in a dogfight for the division… You have to take it one week at a time." Mahomes said after the game, per Charles Goldman.

"Last week we didn't have the fight that we had this week. I thought the fight was better this week. Whenever you're playing up against a really good football team. But at the end a loss is a loss and you learn from it, you move on from it and we're still early in the season." Mahomes continued .

Chiefs Looking to Bounce Back After Second Defeat

This loss marks the Chiefs' fourth to the Broncos out of the last five, the sole win being the opening week of the season back in mid-September.

And coming now off consecutive losses to Seattle and Denver, the emphasis will be on getting back to basics and back on track.

Entering a slightly easier run of games than two of final four teams from last year's playoffs, in the Jets, Falcons and Cardinals , Kansas City will be hoping that 5-2 soon becomes 8-2 before they embark on a brutal five-game stretch that sees them take on the Bills, Rams, Bengals, Patriots and 49ers.

articles.title: Patrick Mahomes Sends Veiled Message to NFL on Chiefs-Broncos Controversy
articles.summary: Patrick Mahomes took a subtle dig at the latest Chiefs-Broncos controversy minutes after Kansas City's loss. The post Patrick Mahomes Sends Veiled Message to...
articles.body:
The Kansas City Chiefs are officially on a losing streak, but for a brief moment it appeared Patrick Mahomes led another magical game-winning drive against the Denver Broncos. Instead, the touchdown was negated as the referees called a false start.

When asked about the controversial call, Mahomes initially attempted to take the high road by backing the call before adding that in game-deciding moments "the little stuff doesn't get called like that."

"I have not seen it, but like it didn't surprise me or catch me or anything like that, so it couldn't have been big, but it was called," Mahomes told reporters on November 1, following the Chiefs' loss to the Broncos.

"I mean, at the end of the day, you have to go with whatever is called, but a lot of times in those big moments the little stuff doesn't get called like that."

Chiefs HC Andy Reid Disagreed With Late Penalty Call vs. Broncos

It is worth noting that Kansas City had another opportunity to score even after the five-yard penalty, but Mahomes was sacked on the final play of the game. Chiefs head coach Andy Reid was a bit more direct about the controversial call.

"I didn't see it," Reid said of the late penalty that negated a potential touchdown, per ESPN's Nate Taylor.

"I saw him move his head, but I didn't see [a false start]."

articles.title: Eagles fall to 2-6 after Commanders score 27 unanswered in Week 8
articles.summary: The Eagles fell 27-10 to Washington after scoring just 10 first-quarter points, extending their losing streak to six games and dropping to 2-6
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles ' losing streak reached six games Sunday night after a promising first quarter gave way to another disappointing offensive performance in a 27-10 loss to the Washington Commanders at Northwest Stadium.

Philadelphia built a 10-0 lead behind a Jake Elliott field goal and Saquon Barkley's 5-yard touchdown run, but Washington scored the final 27 points to improve to 2-4-1 and move ahead of the Eagles in the NFC East standings. Philadelphia dropped to 2-6, its worst start through eight games since 1999, and suffered its sixth consecutive defeat for the first time since 2012.

Tanner McKee completed 23 of 34 passes for 212 yards with an interception, but he was sacked five times and lost a fumble as the Eagles struggled to establish any offensive rhythm after the opening quarter. Philadelphia finished with 268 total yards, converted five of 15 third-down attempts and committed two turnovers.

Eagles waste early opportunity against Washington

Philadelphia appeared to have the momentum after an impressive defensive play from Andrew Mukuba helped create its only touchdown. The second-year safety forced a fumble by Washington tight end Chig Okonkwo, and Zack Baun recovered it, setting up a short touchdown drive capped by Barkley's Wildcat run.

However, the Eagles failed to capitalize on their early advantage. Washington responded with an 11-play, 89-yard touchdown drive that ended with Jayden Daniels finding Stefon Diggs for an 8-yard score. Drew Stevens added a field goal just before halftime to give the Commanders a 13-10 lead.

Washington extended its advantage with another Stevens field goal following McKee's third-quarter fumble. The Eagles later moved into scoring position during a lengthy fourth-quarter possession, but an illegal formation penalty on Jordan Mailata wiped out a successful field goal before Elliott missed the ensuing attempt.

The Commanders added another field goal and sealed the victory after Rasul Douglas intercepted McKee late in the fourth quarter. Rachaad White finished a short touchdown drive, and Washington converted a two-point attempt to complete the scoring.

Eagles offense goes scoreless over final three quarters

The Eagles struggled to establish their running game, finishing with 91 yards on 29 carries. Barkley managed just 30 yards on 13 attempts, while Elijah Mitchell added 34 yards on 11 carries.

Rookie receiver Makai Lemon led Philadelphia with six receptions for 57 yards, while tight end Eli Stowers contributed three catches for 53 yards. Their production provided some encouraging individual performances, but the offense failed to generate consistent scoring opportunities.

Defensively, Jeremiah Trotter Jr. recorded a team-high 10 tackles, while Mukuba finished with nine tackles and a forced fumble. Jalen Carter and Nolan Smith Jr. each recorded a sack, but Washington gained 339 total yards and repeatedly controlled the line of scrimmage.

The Eagles return home to face the New York Giants in Week 9 before their scheduled bye. With their losing streak reaching six and their playoff hopes fading, Philadelphia faces mounting pressure to improve before the season slips further out of reach.

articles.title: Dak Prescott’s blunt admission puts Brian Schottenheimer under pressure after Cowboys loss
articles.summary: Dak Prescott has admitted the Dallas Cowboys needed to be more aggressive during their overtime loss to the Arizona Cardinals, adding to the pressure on head...
articles.body:
Dak Prescott has admitted the Dallas Cowboys needed to be more aggressive during their overtime loss to the Arizona Cardinals, adding to the pressure on head coach Brian Schottenheimer after another disappointing offensive performance.

Dallas managed just 261 total yards in the defeat while its defence gave up 467. The result leaves the Cowboys at 3-5 and raises further questions about their ability to turn the season around.

Prescott completed 19 of 29 passes for 195 yards and a touchdown. He also rushed for 20 yards and another score, but his comments after the game drew attention to the Cowboys' offensive approach.

Dak Prescott wants Brian Schottenheimer to be more aggressive with Dallas Cowboys

Speaking to reporters after the loss, Prescott defended Schottenheimer but admitted he would have preferred a different approach against Arizona.

"Yeah, I wish we would've been more aggressive there."

The quarterback did not directly criticise his head coach, but his admission comes at a difficult time for Schottenheimer. Dallas has struggled offensively in three of its last four games, leaving the coaching staff under increasing scrutiny.

Cowboys owner and general manager Jerry Jones was also questioned about Schottenheimer's position following the defeat. However, Jones insisted the problems extended beyond the head coach.

"That's not in my mind at this time," Jones said. "This is an indictment of the whole show … This is a criticism of everyone."

Jones also acknowledged that he had previously made a mid-season coaching change, referring to Wade Phillips, but dismissed the possibility of doing the same with Schottenheimer.

"I'm not proud of it, but I made a change with Wade Phillips there in the middle of the season," Jones added. "I don't see that here at all."

Despite that reassurance, Jones made it clear that the Cowboys' performances were unacceptable and that responsibility rested with everyone involved.

"Well, I don't know," Jones said when asked whether he was worried about Schottenheimer. "None of us are getting it done and that should be my concern."

The Cowboys now need to find answers quickly, particularly on offence. Prescott remains central to their hopes of recovering from their poor start, but Schottenheimer's play-calling will face further scrutiny if Dallas cannot produce a more convincing performance in its next game.

articles.title: Cowboys’ miserable meltdown vs. Cardinals breaks incredible 69-game streak
articles.summary: You could get hit by a giant asteroid or eaten by a killer whale, and you still would not feel as terrible as the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday. The Cowboys blew...
articles.body:
You could get hit by a giant asteroid or eaten by a killer whale, and you still would not feel as terrible as the Dallas Cowboys on Sunday.

The Cowboys blew a 14-point lead in the fourth quarter and lost to the Arizona Cardinals, 33-30, in overtime, much to the sheer despair of the home crowd at AT&T Stadium.

Chad Ryland kicked the game-winning field goal from 42 yards, redeeming himself after failing to convert the extra point that would have finished off the Cowboys in regulation. Arizona and Dallas each have a 3-5 record.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

According to ESPN's Todd Archer, the Cowboys snapped a decades-long streak after their monumental collapse.

"Before Sunday, the Cowboys were 69-0 since 2000 when leading by 14 points or more in the fourth quarter. They are now 69-1," wrote Archer on X.

Dak Prescott went 19-of-29 for 195 yards and one touchdown. He was sacked four times. He scored on a rush at the 14:20 mark of the fourth quarter to increase Dallas' lead to 24-10.

In a report from the Associated Press' Schuyler Dixon, Prescott admitted that it was "very disappointing."

"One of the toughest (losses), I guess, I've been a part of. No other words for it really, other than really, really disappointing, frustrating. It's part of this league," said the veteran quarterback.

The Cowboys allowed 467 yards, including 80 yards in eight plays in the closing minute of regulation.

Despite the painful loss and the mediocre campaign, owner Jerry Jones said he is not keen on firing anybody .

The Cowboys will battle the Indianapolis Colts in Week 9.

articles.title: Bills DL Ed Oliver’s heartwarming message on how teammates helped him through offseason tragedy

articles.body:
The Buffalo Bills finally got Ed Oliver back for their Week 8 clash against the Baltimore Ravens. The defensive lineman had missed the last month due to a knee injury against the New England Patriots. Oliver certainly made his presence felt as he had three quarterback hits to help the Bills to a 36-10 win against the quarterback-depleted Ravens .

"A lot of them don't know it, but some days I don't be feeling too high. I come to that D-line room, and you've got guys like Zane Durant that just put a smile on my face. And Big Boy, I'm talking about Deone (Walker), and TJ (Parker) and the different personalities in the D-line room that really lift my spirits when sometimes I'm not really all the way there," Oliver said.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Losing a child is one of the most painful things anyone can experience in life. Thankfully for Oliver, he has a support system in that Bills D-line room that can help him in some ways cope with the unbearable loss of a loved one.

It's not every day that a rugged football player gets honest about mental health. That's why it's heartwarming to hear Oliver be vulnerable and show his appreciation to his friends on the team for all they've done for him during these difficult times.

articles.title: Uninspired LAFC drops regular season home finale to Minnesota United FC
articles.summary: Los Angeles looked flat and lacked energy, suffering a disappointing loss in front of the home fans.
articles.body:
LOS ANGELES -- There was an opportunity on Sunday evening for LAFC to gain three important points as they push for a top four finish in the Western Conference. Doing so would provide home-field advantage in the opening round, best-of-three series of the MLS Cup Playoffs. Instead, they put forth a lackluster effort, falling 3-1 to Minnesota United FC at BMO Stadium.

It was Minnesota's first victory against the Black & Gold in Los Angeles since 2019. LA finished with a 9-4-4 record in their 17 home games this season, with one final match remaining on the road before postseason play begins.

"I am responsible. I am not happy," interim head coach Xavi Tamarit said. "All of us, we are very disappointed with this game...we want to say sorry to the people who were in the stadium, who were watching us on the TV, because this is not the team we want to show."

LAFC got off to a slow start from the beginning, stringing together a disorganized attack and failing to generate any real chances through the opening 30 minutes. The defense held firm for most of that stretch, holding Minnesota without a shot attempt through its first 28 minutes.

Midfielder Joaquín Pereyra, with his squad's first attempt of the match, made it a 1-0 game in favor of the visitors in minute 29. He took advantage of a well-placed throw-in from defender Cherrion Valerius, which dropped down perfectly in front of Pereyra as he rocketed his shot past Hugo Lloris.

Minnesota United FC midfielder Joaquín Pereyra (26) smiles during the first half of an MLS soccer match against LAFC at BMO Stadium, Sunday, Nov. 1, 2026, in Los Angeles.

Valerius kept the momentum rolling in Minnesota's favor, adding a score of his own just five minutes later. He used his run to meet a header from forward Kelvin Yeboah and volley it over the top of Lloris to make the score 2-0.

The second half was no different. LAFC continued to look stagnant and impatient. Their runs came across as forced, and the quality of chances did not get any better until the late stages.

Denis Bouanga, Son Heung-min and the rest of the attack simply lacked the composure and cohesiveness to turn their luck around and claw back. There would be no repeat of the 2-0 lead that they erased last Sunday against the LA Galaxy.

Pereyra scored the dagger goal in the 81st minute to earn himself a brace, drilling a left-footed strike from distance that Lloris could not get to in time with his diving attempt. It was just the second time since May 17 that LA has surrendered three goals in a single match.

Despite the overall disappointment that flowed through BMO Stadium on Sunday, Sergio Vásquez provided what was perhaps the flashiest goal of the season for LAFC to prevent a shutout. He leapt into the air, firing a bicycle kick strike that just managed to sneak past Minnesota goalkeeper Drake Callender.

"It's a little uncomfortable given the defeat," said Vásquez of his goal. "I think there was some errors in that game that is not characteristic of us as a team, but there are things that we need to correct and get better at. As far as the goal goes, it's the first bicycle kick in my career. It's a very beautiful moment for me in my career, so I'm happy and grateful for that moment."

It was Vásquez's first goal as a member of the Black & Gold, coming in minute 90 to help avoid the club's first scoreless outing since Sept. 26.

Just one match remains in the regular season, with LAFC set to face off against the Seattle Sounders at Lumen Field next Saturday, Nov. 7. LA defeated Seattle 1-0 in their first meeting of the year on May 24, but the home side will be highly motivated this time around. The Sounders sit just one spot out of a Wild Card spot in the Western Conference.

"Of course I am not happy with that performance, but I am not so worried because every team can have one bad day," Tamarit said. "What we cannot do is not reflect, not learn. Because if we learn, it can be a good medicine before playoffs. If we don't learn, we will be in trouble."

For LAFC, concern remains about consistency. Consecutive wins haven't come since late July, and Tamarit has coached his club to only a single victory in five tries. Time is running thin, and the postseason looms, whether LA can prove that it's poised for it or not.

articles.title: Eagles get wrecked by Commanders in epic meltdown: Nick Sirianni is on hot seat— what happens next?
articles.summary: The Eagles were blown out by Commanders. Can Nick Sirianni survive this?
articles.body:
LANDOVER, Md. — The Eagles have expressed confidence that they could dig themselves out of a 2-5 hole to save their season, but the team shouldn't believe that anymore.

The Eagles dropped their sixth consecutive game on Sunday night in a 27-10 loss to the Washington Commanders at Northwest Stadium. Now, the 2-6 Eagles have the worst record in the NFC East and have almost no shot of making the playoffs.

The Eagles are one of the NFL's worst teams. In a few months, the organization could make major changes during the offseason to get the team back on track.

Will Eagles coach Nick Sirianni escape this nightmare season?

If the Eagles continue to play this poorly, the team could move in another direction after the season. Sirianni is squarely on the hot seat.

Here are NJ.com's takeaways from the Eagles' 17-point loss vs. the Commanders:

The concern heading into Week 8 was Philadelphia's defense would spiral after giving up 38 points to the Cowboys last week and collapse down the stretch.

In the second quarter, Commanders wide receiver Stefon Diggs capped off an 11-play, 89-yard drive by reeling in an eight-yard touchdown over Eagles safety Kenny Moore. Moore gave up the touchdown because he was flat-footed in coverage.

On Washington's final scoring drive of the first half, the Eagles left Diggs wide open on a crossing route, and he racked up 20 yards on the catch-and-run to Philadelphia's 30-yard line.

Washington kicked a field goal on that drive, but Washington's offense could have caused more damage. Daniels missed a touchdown throw to Okonkwo, who was wide open near the 20-yard line.

With 2:51 remaining in the third quarter, Eagles All-Pro cornerback Quinyon Mitchell was beaten downfield by Treylon Burks on a 53-yard catch to Philadelphia's seven-yard line.

Philadelphia's defense struggled for most of the game, but it had some good moments, too, including making a third-down stop from the seven-yard line to hold Washington to a field goal.

With 5:34 remaining in the first quarter, second-year Eagles safety Drew Mukuba knocked the ball out of Commanders tight end Chigoziem Okonkwo's hands for a fumble, and it was recovered by Eagles linebacker Zack Baun at Washington's 26-yard line. Four plays later, the Eagles scored their first touchdown of the game.

Some progress, but the Eagles' offense is still bad

For the second consecutive week, the Eagles showed some promise on offense, but the product still wasn't very good.

Eagles quarterback Tanner McKee completed 23 of 34 passes for 212 yards. He also threw an interception.

The Eagles only finished with 91 rushing yards. Star running back Saquon Barkley was not explosive because he played through back and hamstring injuries. He finished with 13 carries for 30 yards.

Philadelphia's offensive line gave up five sacks for 35 yards.

The Eagles' best offensive moments came in the first half.

On the Eagles' first scoring drive, McKee threw over the second level of Washington's defense to rookie wide receiver Makai Lemon, and two plays later, he connected with Darius Cooper over the middle for 11 yards. Those two throws set up Jake Elliott's 40-yard field goal.

On the Eagles' first touchdown drive, McKee completed a 24-yard pass to Barkley on a wheel route, moving the ball to Washington's 2-yard line. Then, two plays later, Barkley rushed for a three-yard touchdown on a direct snap.

These moments were encouraging, but the Eagles played poorly on most of their offensive drives.

Philadelphia's offensive momentum was stalled during the second quarter, when Commanders defensive tackle Shy Tuttle sacked McKee for a seven-yard loss. The Eagles had the ball inside Washington's 50-yard line, but that sack forced them to punt.

In the third quarter, Commanders edge rusher Charles Omenihu snuck past Eagles center Drew Kendall and sacked McKee for a five-yard loss on first down. That offensive drive ended when Commanders edge rusher Dorance Armstrong beat Eagles rookie offensive tackle Markel Bell and strip-sacked McKee. Omenihu recovered the fumble.

With 8:56 remaining in the fourth quarter, Bell jumped offsides on fourth-and-4, drawing a five-yard penalty. The Eagles kept the offense on the field, but Bell's mistake forced them to a kick field goal.

Elliott's kick from 41 yards hit the left goal post and fell wide for a miss.

Commanders wide receiver Luke McCaffrey returned the opening kickoff for 44 yards after running through a gaping hole in the Eagles' coverage.

Philadelphia's punt coverage unit gave up a 27-yard return with one minute remaining in the second quarter. McCaffrey was on the other end again. The Eagles gave up too much room in the middle of the field. The Commanders took advantage of the good field position and made a go-ahead field goal before halftime.

Philadelphia's special teams struggles are small compared to the team's other issues, but they still hurt the team.

articles.title: Brooklyn Nets Finally Break Through Behind Michael Porter Jr.
articles.summary: The Brooklyn Nets entered Sunday’s game winless at 0-5. The Nets defeated the Indiana Pacers 98-90 to give them their first win on the season. Michael Porter...
articles.body:
The Brooklyn Nets entered Sunday's game winless at 0-5. The Nets defeated the Indiana Pacers 98-90 to give them their first win on the season. Michael Porter Jr. led the way with 23 points and 9 rebounds in the game. Day'Ron Sharpe and Julius Randle both contributed to the win in a big way as well. Randle added 20 points and Sharpe finished with a double-double, 15 points and 13 rebounds.

Brooklyn Nets Forward, Michael Porter Jr. Shines

Porter shot 7/16 from the field and made 3 three-pointers for his 23 points. He was also aggressive and able to get to the free-throw line, he made 6 of his 9 attempts. He played a very well-rounded game adding 9 rebounds and 3 assists as well. 13 of his 23 points came in the first half and he showed what type of night it was going to be. Porter is one of those players that when he gets hot it becomes nearly impossible to stop.

He is 6'10 with a high release which makes it nearly impossible to block his shot. It was a three point Nets lead in the third quarter when Porter made a three and was fouled. That play went from 43-40 to 47-40 and gave Brooklyn all the momentum. Shortly after that play, the Nets found themselves up 12 and it became hard for the Pacers to catch back up.

There were three players that stepped up in a big way for the Nets outside of Porter. Those players were Randle, Sharpe, and Nolan Traore. Randle had 20 points, Sharpe had 15 points and 13 rebounds, and Traore finished the game with 16 points and 6 assists. The Nets needed every single one of them to maintain their lead. They were all scoring, playmaking, and rebounding.

The overall production that Brooklyn got for this game is something they hope they can get every game. Traore especially, he showed something that the Nets will need going forward. Everyone knows what Sharpe and Randle are capable of, but Traore was solid all-around. He was finding the open guy, scoring and playing defense. Traore was a bright spot for Brooklyn and is a player they will need going forward.

Brooklyn finally got all the pressure off of being one of the last two winless teams. During this game, they showed better discipline on defense and more patience on offense. They were struggling to get multiple players to be able to contribute offensively and finally got it. This gives Coach Jordi Fernandez something to build on in the upcoming games.

He was able to see what personnel he's able to use on both ends of the floor. Traore may have earned himself more responsibility too with the way he was able to defend and play on offense. This was a good win for the Nets and they are no longer winless.

This was just one win, but it's something to build on going forward. Brooklyn has a lot of bright spots with their young players. These guys are going to be really good in the near future. The Nets show signs of what they can be, and if they can get consistent, then they can win some games.

articles.title: Instant analysis of Eagles' 27-10 loss to Commanders in Week 8
articles.summary: Instant analysis of the Eagles' 27-10 loss to Washington, including Tanner McKee's struggles, poor pass protection and a sixth straight defeat
articles.body:
The Philadelphia Eagles entered Sunday night's matchup against the Washington Commanders needing a performance that could restore confidence in a struggling team. Instead, a 27-10 defeat exposed many of the same problems that have defined their six-game losing streak.

Philadelphia led 10-0 in the opening quarter but failed to score again, allowing Washington to control the final three quarters and turn another nationally televised matchup into a lopsided defeat. The Eagles finished with 268 total yards, committed two turnovers, and struggled to protect Tanner McKee consistently.

The loss dropped Philadelphia to 2-6 and raised further questions about whether the team's offensive personnel, execution, and overall approach can produce a meaningful turnaround.

Offensive limitations remain impossible to ignore

McKee completed 23 of 34 passes for 212 yards, but the final numbers do not fully capture the struggles of Philadelphia's passing game. Washington recorded five sacks and regularly disrupted the quarterback's timing, leaving the Eagles unable to capitalize on manageable situations.

The offensive line struggled with pressure throughout the night, and penalties made matters worse. A costly strip-sack ended a promising third-quarter possession, while an illegal formation penalty later erased a successful fourth-quarter field goal.

Philadelphia also failed to establish a physical rushing attack. Saquon Barkley carried 13 times for 30 yards, while Elijah Mitchell added 34 yards on 11 attempts. The Eagles averaged just 3.1 yards per carry, repeatedly forcing McKee into situations that favored Washington's defense.

Defense creates early opportunity but cannot sustain momentum

The Eagles' best defensive moment came when Andrew Mukuba forced a fumble that Zack Baun recovered, creating the short field for Barkley's touchdown. Philadelphia also received sacks from Jalen Carter and Nolan Smith Jr., while Jeremiah Trotter Jr. finished with 10 tackles.

However, Washington regrouped after its difficult start. Jayden Daniels threw for 217 yards and a touchdown, while the Commanders rushed for 135 yards and averaged 5.2 yards per carry.

Philadelphia struggled to win early downs consistently and keep Washington from controlling possession. The Commanders' 89-yard touchdown drive in the second quarter demonstrated the defense's inability to sustain the momentum created by its early takeaway.

The Eagles' problems extend beyond a single quarterback or position group. Philadelphia has now lost six consecutive games, including back-to-back prime-time defeats to division opponents, and the offense continues to struggle with execution and situational awareness.

The upcoming matchup against the New York Giants presents another opportunity to reverse the slide, but the team must first address the mistakes that have repeatedly undermined otherwise competitive stretches.

The Eagles remain mathematically alive in the NFC East, yet their recent performance provides little reason to assume a turnaround is imminent. With a bye approaching, Sirianni and his staff face difficult questions about what must change before the remainder of the season.

articles.title: Rams’ Sean McVay not on the same page as LA president when it comes to Chargers rivalry
articles.summary: The Los Angeles Rams took care of business against the Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday, but Sean McVay and team president Kevin Demoff apparently have very d...
articles.body:
The Los Angeles Rams took care of business against the Los Angeles Chargers on Sunday, but Sean McVay and team president Kevin Demoff apparently have very different views on the crosstown matchup.

After the Rams' 24-9 win at SoFi Stadium , McVay was asked whether he considers the Chargers a rival. His answer was short and to the point.

"Kevin Demoff does. I don't," McVay said, via Gary Klein of the Los Angeles Times.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Demoff, for his part, did not hide his excitement about the result. The Rams president celebrated on X with a GIF of Will Ferrell's Ron Burgundy from "Anchorman" saying, "That's amazing," which ESPN's Adam Schefter later shared.

McVay's comments are not surprising. The Rams and Chargers have both called Los Angeles home since relocating about a decade ago and now share SoFi Stadium, but they rarely see each other. The NFL schedule pairs the two teams only about once every four years, and Sunday's game was just their second meeting since the stadium opened in 2020.

Their facilities are also far apart, with the Rams practicing in the western San Fernando Valley and the Chargers based more than 30 miles away in El Segundo.

McVay also made it clear before the game that he was not overlooking the winless Chargers.

"I really couldn't care less what the record says," McVay said last week . "I see a team that's really good. They've had a chance to win a lot of these games."

The Chargers made it a game for a half. They led 9-3 behind three Cameron Dicker field goals before Kyren Williams punched in a 1-yard touchdown run late in the second quarter to give Los Angeles a 10-9 halftime lead.

The Rams took over from there. Blake Corum broke free for a 23-yard touchdown run early in the third quarter, and Matthew Stafford found Puka Nacua for an 18-yard score to make it 24-9. The defense did the rest, intercepting the Chargers twice and recording two sacks while holding them scoreless after halftime.

The win improved the Rams to 4-4 and gave them their second straight victory. The Chargers, meanwhile, remain winless .

Whether McVay calls it a rivalry or not, the Rams now hold an 8-6 edge in the all-time series. They will visit the Washington Commanders next Sunday.

Philadelphia Eagles TE Dallas Goedert finished with 30 yards on four receptions during the team's Week 8 loss to the Washington Commanders .

Why It Matters: Goedert entered play on Sunday night with an elite matchup -- only the Lions had allowed more fantasy points to tight ends than the Commanders. He'd also had great success (4-77-2) versus Washington back in Week 1. With Tanner McKee under center instead of Jalen Hurts, however, the offense was stuck in the mud for much of the game. As a result, Goedert's production dipped to 4-30-0. In three games with McKee as QB1, Goedert has totaled 15 receptions, 139 yards, and no TDs. That's middling TE2 production, at best. Until the Eagles start looking more competent offensively, Goedert should be remanded to your bench.

articles.title: Nolan Traore lifts Nets to first win of season with big second half
articles.summary: The Brooklyn Nets needed a lift on Sunday against the shorthanded Indiana Pacers as they sought their first win of the season. Sophomore point guard Nolan Tr...
articles.body:
The Brooklyn Nets needed a lift on Sunday against the shorthanded Indiana Pacers as they sought their first win of the season. Sophomore point guard Nolan Traore answered the call.

After an ugly first half in which the Nets scored 43 points on 15-of-39 shooting (38.5 percent), Traore sparked the offense. The French Floor general scored a team-high 14 points and drained four threes during the second half, lifting Brooklyn to a 98-90 victory. He finished the game with six assists and one turnover.

"The difference was just us moving the ball well and trying to find the best shot every time, and also being consistent on defense. That's the main thing," Traore said. "I think [the difference for me] was just like great spacing. I know that they want to double Julius [Randle], so we take advantage of this. And we made shots also. We did a great job. I'm happy and proud of my teammates."

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

General Manager Sean Marks has said he is "looking for the next Nets." Traore is among the team's most promising young prospects, alongside Egor Demin and Mikel Brown Jr.

After adding noticeable muscle this offseason, the 20-year-old has impressed. He's averaged 14.3 points on .467/.389/.727 shooting splits, with 4.0 assists and 2.0 turnovers per game across his last four outings.

Traore has started the Nets' last three games. Brooklyn was without Demin (right leg contusion) and Brown (back injury management) on Sunday.

Nets grind out ugly victory over Pacers on back of Nolan Traore's big second half

Michael Porter Jr. led the Nets with 23 points, nine rebounds and three assists in the victory, while Julius Randle added 20 points, five rebounds and six assists. The duo combined for 12-of-31 shooting while turning the ball over eight times. They know that won't be enough in coming games, but they did enough down the stretch Sunday to pick up a much-needed victory.

"It wasn't a pretty win, but it's a win regardless. We got that zero out of that column, so we're really happy about that," Porter said. "If you're going to be a good team, eventually you've got to learn how to win games like this. Neither team shot the ball well. Neither team cracked 100 points. That's the type of games we want to win. It was good resilience. Sometimes, we let bad offense dictate our defense, and [Sunday,] we just kept going, grinding it out."

The Nets shot 30-of-73 (41.1 percent) from the field and 13-of-39 (33.3 percent) from three with 21 assists and 15 turnovers. Meanwhile, the Pacers could not find an offensive rhythm without Tyrese Haliburton , Ivica Zubac, T.J. McConnell and Obi Toppin. They finished the game shooting 28-of-70 (40 percent) with 21 assists and 14 turnovers.

With Zubac sidelined, Day'Ron Sharpe delivered his best performance of the season after a slow start. The Nets big man posted 15 points, 13 rebounds and four assists on 5-of-7 shooting in 26 minutes.

"[Day'Ron was] unbelievable," said head coach Jordi Fernandez. "He was big on the boards. He did a little bit of everything. He made his [only] three. He set screens. I'm very happy for him. We don't win this game without him. And the reality is how much he cares about winning and impacting winning. And this game… I think that [stat] line is impressive. So all his energy and willingness to do the right things paid off."

Moe Wagner added 14 points and six rebounds on 4-of-6 shooting in 21 minutes off the bench.

The Nets will be back in action on Monday against the New York Knicks at Madison Square Garden.

articles.title: Dolphins’ Malik Willis gives honest assessment of Patriots’ defense after Week 8 loss
articles.summary: Malik Willis got real on how the New England defense kept him and the Miami offense in check following the Dolphins’ 24-19 loss to the Patriots on Sunday eve...
articles.body:
Malik Willis got real on how the New England defense kept him and the Miami offense in check following the Dolphins' 24-19 loss to the Patriots on Sunday evening.

Willis is halfway through the fifth season of his NFL career, his first with the Dolphins. This marks his first year as a full-time starter, being a key leader in Miami's rebuilding offense.

Miami is going through a brutal start to the season, finally getting their first win after beating the New York Jets. However, they returned to the loss column after falling to the Patriots. Willis reflected on the loss after the game, per reporter Joe Schad. He gave props to the New England defense for playing more man-to-man coverage than zone coverage, limiting the options Miami had on offense.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

"I think they did a good job. All credit to the defense, all credit to the Patriots. We just got to continue to figure out what we're going to do as far as adjustments go, as far as how we want to attack different schemes," Willis said.

How Malik Willis, Dolphins played against Patriots

Malik Willis and the Dolphins have a lot of work to do in their rebuild. Learning how to manage adjustments from opponents like what the Patriots did to them will be one of those lessons.

Miami initially had the upper hand over New England, taking a 13-3 lead at halftime. However, the Patriots roared back with a 21-6 display in the last 30 minutes of regulation.

Willis had a decent display leading Miami's offense before New England contained him in the second half. He completed 21 out of 32 passes for 211 yards and two touchdowns and one interception.

Ollie Gordon II was the standout in the run game, racking up 19 carries for 69 yards. Kevin Coleman Jr. led receivers with 46 yards and a touchdown on three catches. Greg Dulcih and Caleb Douglas both had four receptions for 43 yards, while Malik Washington caught five passes for 40 yards and a touchdown.

The Dolphins look to bounce back in their next home matchup. They host the Detroit Lions as kickoff commences on Nov. 8 at 1 p.m. ET.

articles.title: How will Wales fare on Nations Championship return?
articles.summary: BBC Sport Wales provides a recap of what has happened so far in the inaugural Nations Championship and what will occur during the next month?
articles.body:
Wales will start their international season next weekend when they return to the Nations Championship.

Steve Tandy's side face four games as they host Japan, New Zealand and Australia in Cardiff, before a final play-off match at the Allianz Stadium completes the November schedule.

The autumn games begin the road to the 2027 World Cup in Australia in a year's time.

BBC Sport Wales provides a recap of what has happened so far in the inaugural running of the global tournament and looks at what lies in wait over the next month.

The Nations Championship pits the northern hemisphere teams who compete in the Six Nations - England, Ireland, Scotland, Wales, France and Italy - against southern hemisphere giants South Africa, New Zealand, Australia and Argentina, plus invited sides Fiji and Japan.

All teams play each of the six nations in the opposing hemisphere once, with three rounds of fixtures having already been staged in July and now another three in November.

Their results will rank the teams within their own hemisphere, from one to six, before a final play-off weekend at the Allianz Stadium in Twickenham.

How have Wales fared so far and who do they play next?

Wales will resume the Nations Championship in fifth place in the northern hemisphere standings after a mixed July campaign.

It started with an encouraging six-try victory against Fiji at the Cardiff City Stadium, which was considered a home venue for the Pacific Islanders side.

But Wales faltered during a demanding travelling schedule as they were outclassed by Argentina in San Juan and thrashed by South Africa in Durban.

Now they face a trio of home games in Cardiff with the opening match staged against Eddie Jones' Japan side, who also sit fifth in their table, with the two teams potentially meeting twice this November.

The tests will become harder when Dave Rennie brings his New Zealand side to Cardiff on 14 November, before the Wallabies arrive seven days later.

Saturday, 11 July: Argentina 35-21 Wales

Saturday, 18 July: South Africa 43-0 Wales

Saturday, 7 November: Wales v Japan, Principality Stadium, Cardiff, 16:40 GMT

Saturday, 14 November: Wales v New Zealand, Principality Stadium, Cardiff, 14:10 GMT

Saturday, 21 November: Wales v Australia, Principality Stadium, Cardiff, 20:10 GMT.

Uncapped Dragons duo Aneurin Owen and Che Hope, and Cardiff prop Rhys Barrett were named in a 39-strong group for the November Tests, with hooker Dewi Lake again handed the captaincy.

Head coach Tandy called up Dragons lock Seb Davies and Cardiff number eight Taine Basham for the first time since he took charge of the national side in September 2025.

Dragons wing Rio Dyer initially earned a recall, but was ruled out because of a hamstring injury and replaced by uncapped Scarlets back Macs Page.

Leicester flanker Tommy Reffell and scrum-half Kieran Hardy were among the notable absentees because of injury, while veteran number eight Taulupe Faletau is also absent.

Fifteen of the players are based outside of Wales with 14 plying their club trade in England and Montpellier lock Adam Beard based in France.

Forwards: Rhys Barratt, Rhys Carre, Nicky Smith, Gareth Thomas, Dewi Lake (capt), Liam Belcher, Ryan Elias, Tomas Francis, Archie Griffin, Dillon Lewis, Adam Beard, Ben Carter, Seb Davies, Dafydd Jenkins, Teddy Williams, Taine Basham, James Botham, Kane James, Alex Mann, Jac Morgan, Taine Plumtree, Aaron Wainwright.

Backs: Che Hope, Reuben Morgan-Williams, Tomos Williams, Sam Costelow, Dan Edwards, Joe Hawkins, Louie Hennessey, Eddie James, Max Llewellyn, Aneurin Owen, Josh Adams, Macs Page, Gabriel Hamer-Webb, Ellis Mee, Blair Murray, Louis Rees-Zammit, Tom Rogers.

Early indications suggest there could empty seats at the Principality Stadium this autumn.

A look at the WRU website shows a significant amount of tickets still available for the three home matches.

The first test for Wales will be to match the 61,000 crowd that witnessed the dramatic 24-23 win against Japan 12 months ago.

Wales should expect a sellout against the All Blacks, especially given the favourable Saturday mid-afternoon kick-off time, although the late evening start against Australia a week later will provide its challenges.

The attendances will give an insight into whether the upheaval in Welsh rugby has affected interest in the game - or whether apathy is setting in.

The Wales players are again performing amid the backdrop of an uncertain domestic future with the WRU currently determined to stick to its policy of cutting Ospreys or Scarlets by 2028.

There will be an annual general meeting (AGM) held a day after Wales play Australia, while a rugby summit featuring the professional sides will be staged in December.

Ticket sales are important because they form more than 50% of the annual turnover of the WRU, who announced an £18m loss earlier this month.

What happens at the final weekend at Twickenham?

On the final weekend in November, there is a three-day play-off event staged at Allianz Stadium in Twickenham.

The sixth-placed team in the northern hemisphere plays off against the equivalent in the southern hemisphere standings and so on, culminating in the two top-ranked sides taking each other on.

On Friday evening the sixth-placed and third-place finishers will face each other, while Saturday will see the fifth-place and second place matches.

The Sunday finale will see the fourth-placed sides compete before the winner of that final match between the top seeds crowned the inaugural Nations Championship winner.

There is also a parallel, Ryder-Cup style, hemisphere title.

The winner of each of the matches on the play-offs weekend will earn one point for their hemisphere, except for the contest between the two top-ranked teams which delivers two.

The first hemisphere to earn four points over the weekend will be crowned winners.

Sixth-place North v Sixth-place South (16:40 GMT)

Third-place North v Third-place South (20:10 GMT)

Fifth-place North v Fifth-place South (13:10 GMT)

Second-place North v Second-place South (16:40 GMT)

Fourth-place North v Fourth-place South (13:10 GMT)

First-place North v First-place South (16:40 GMT).
